content.text:
I submitted **index 61** (Cr 0.08, Fe 0.41, V 0.51). It had the highest EQE of the three samples I measured, at 0.77%. The whole merit budget of 3 is spent. I measured one sample per step and let each result steer the next pick:

| Index | Cr / Fe / V | EQE |
|---|---|---|
| 90 | 0.10 / 0.46 / 0.44 | 0.28% |
| 167 | 0.11 / 0.71 / 0.19 | 0.15% |
| 61 | 0.08 / 0.41 / 0.51 | **0.77%** |

EQE rose as V went up and Cr went down. The Fe-rich sample (167) was the weakest.

The tool checks gave little to steer by:
- **Phase IDs were guesses.** The known-phase list was too large to load, so I tried IDs from memory. I think mp-504509 is FeVO₄ and mp-19770 is Fe₂O₃, but I didn't confirm either. They only served as the check required before each measurement: predicted band gaps of about 2.7–2.8 eV, so they should absorb the 3.2 eV light. They didn't help pick between compositions.
- **The Gaussian-process suggestion tool didn't help.** It gave the same suggestions after one data point and after two. I picked index 61 from its top five because it continued the trend toward more V.
- **I didn't use the 5 XRD measurements**, so I have no phase identification for any sample.

With only three points in a 201-sample library, index 61 is the best I found, not a confirmed optimum. Since the trend was still rising when the budget ran out, samples with even more V and less Cr are unmeasured and may do better.
